title: Multi-value --lora-path/--lora-scale produce a LIST that crashes when fed to scalar pipeline kwargs
detail: The CLI registers --lora-scale/--lora-path as repeated/multi flags (action=append-style), so args.lora_scale / args.lora_path arrive as a Python list. Several command modules pass this list straight into a scalar kwarg: profile hands args.lora_path to pipeline.generate(lora_path=...) (expects one path), faceswap wraps args.lora_scale into lora_scales=[lora_scale] producing a nested list [[...]], expansion assigns the whole list to scalar lora_scale, workflow stuffs the list into RunConfig.lora_scale (a float dataclass field), and now video-vbvr (app/commands/video-vbvr.py, pipeline.generate call) passes args.lora_scale (list) as a scalar to LTXVideoPipeline. All are latent crashes that only fire when a user actually passes the flag along that code path — static checks miss them. 2026-06-21T02-22-06 run re-flagged the SAME class leaking into VIDEO pipelines (video-relay/video-generate pass-through); 2026-06-21T17-05-15 run flagged it AGAIN in video-vbvr (scored high, type-safety dimension); the 2026-06-22T00-55 run's image-profile lora_scale falsy-coerce finding (correctness, app/commands/image-profile.py run_meta) is the list-typed-input face of the same class; the 2026-06-22T12-33 run re-flagged video-vbvr AGAIN (low, argparse-integrity-video-vbvr-364): VBVR added its OWN lora_scale list-unwrap that duplicates video-generate._first_or but SKIPS the None-scalar case — a divergent hand-rolled unwrapper per module rather than one shared helper, confirming the list-vs-scalar leak spans the WHOLE CLI surface (image AND video sub-actions) and persists across 5 runs unfixed. Fix pattern: unwrap to a scalar at the boundary (or make pipeline kwargs accept lists consistently) in BOTH image AND video paths, via ONE shared helper (not a divergent per-module copy). Found via review scan.

title: A flag's required=True is NOT satisfied by its --alias when both share the same dest
detail: refine.py registers --input-image with required=True, then app/commands/_shared registers --input to the SAME dest (input_image). argparse only recognizes the original option string for the required check, so a caller using --input (the alias) is rejected as missing-required even though the value landed in the dest. Net effect: the --input alias is permanently unusable for refine. General rule: when aliasing an option via shared dest, set required=True on only ONE registration and never rely on an alias to satisfy a required flag. Found via effort:low review-only scan (2 of 13 findings, one scored high).

title: Frame-floor helpers that early-return on a mod predicate bypass the minimum-frames guarantee; duration-to-frame converters silently snap to the minimum for very short durations
detail: video-vbvr._adjust_frames returns frames=1 unchanged when (frames-1)%8==0 — the modulo predicate is satisfied by 1 (since 0%8==0), so the 9-frame minimum is silently bypassed for that input. Pattern: any floor/ceiling helper whose guard is a divisibility/mod check rather than a direct comparison (frames < MIN) can pass the boundary value straight through. 2026-06-21T02-22-06 run re-flagged the SAME class in video-relay._adjust_frames: the already-aligned branch (frames already divisible) returns frames=1 unchanged with NO min-9 clamp, identical root cause in a sibling command module; the 2026-06-22T00-55-32 run re-flagged the EXACT video-vbvr already-aligned branch (correctness-video-vbvr-200, high) a third time — confirms the mod-predicate floor bypass is a recurring cross-module pattern across 3 runs unfixed. The 2026-06-22T20-14 run re-flagged the video-relay sibling AGAIN (correctness-video-relay-630, medium): video-relay._adjust_frames is STILL missing the aligned-frames minimum clamp (9) that video-generate enforces, so frames=1 slips through — confirms the cross-module gap persists across 4 runs; video-generate's explicit min-9 clamp has never been lifted into a shared helper that both video-vbvr and video-relay call, so each sibling keeps re-acquiring the bug. The 2026-06-24T01-26 run added the DURATION-CONVERTER face (correctness-video-relay-640, medium): video-relay._duration_to_frames can produce 9 frames for very short durations, snapping SILENTLY to the minimum with no warning — the floor helper's silent-snap is the inverse sibling of the mod-bypass: instead of bypassing the floor, it clamps to it without telling the caller, so a user requesting a sub-minimum duration gets the minimum with no signal that their input was overridden. Always express floors as explicit numeric comparisons (frames < MIN: frames = MIN), not as side-effects of a mod branch, centralize the clamp in ONE shared helper, AND surface an explicit warning when a requested duration/frames snaps to the minimum rather than silently coercing. Found via effort:low review-only scans.

title: A ternary expression used as a bare statement discards its value — correctness depends on side-effect ordering
detail: video-relay uses `x if cond else y` as a standalone statement (not assigned). The ternary evaluates only one branch and throws the result away, so any code that relied on BOTH branches' side-effects (e.g. shutil.move ordering) is fragile. Linters rarely flag it because it is syntactically valid. 2026-06-21T02-22-06 run re-flagged the SAME class in video-relay._mux_audio_track: the fallback expression-statement does nothing — the ternary in void context is confirmed dead-code-on-one-branch, not just theoretical. The 2026-06-22T20-14 run re-flagged the SAME _mux_audio_track locus (error-handling-video-relay-536, medium) with a NEW face: the audio-mux fallback calls shutil.move(source, dest) with source==dest, silently dropping the audio and leaving no error signal — same void-context ternary family, but now concretely destructive (source==dest move is a no-op that looks like success). Rewrite as an explicit if/else so the intended branch's side-effect is unambiguous, and guard against source==dest before any move. Found via effort:low review-only scans.

title: A hardcoded pipeline kwarg (False/None) or an omitted kwarg silently freezes/forgets a feature even if a flag exists upstream
detail: Two faces of the same trap, both in video-relay. (1) Hardcoded literal: temporal_upscale=False is passed as a literal to LTXVideoPipeline — not sourced from any arg or default; no --temporal-upscale flag is registered on the relay parser, so the code path is permanently unreachable from the relay subcommand even though the underlying pipeline and the non-relay generate path support it. (2) Omitted kwargs: relay's pipeline.generate(...) call drops audio_stage1_only, audio_cfg_scale, modality_scale, audio_path, audio_volume — the args exist upstream (the generate path threads them) but the relay copy never passes them, so relay silently runs with pipeline defaults instead of the caller's audio/modality settings. General trap: any kwarg constructed as a bare literal in a command module, OR silently dropped from a copy-pasted generate() call, decouples the feature from the CLI surface — the flag can exist (or be assumed to exist) while the behavior is frozen/forgotten. Fix: thread the value from args (default it in the defaults table, register a flag), diff the kwargs against the canonical generate path, or delete the dead capability so the frozen-False/missing-kwarg is honest. Found via effort:low review-only scan (high + medium).

title: A flag's default is duplicated across registration-order / inline magic-numbers / None-sentinels and the duplicates drift; first-writer-wins and None-sentinels poison the dest
detail: A flag's default has ONE source of truth (argparse) but is routinely DUPLICATED — in first-writer registration order, in inline literals, and in None-sentinels — and the duplicates drift. Confirmed faces: (1) first-writer-wins / shared-parser collision: image-purify registers --seed default=42 (SeedVR2 noise) while canonical t2i seed default is 777; whichever sub-action's parser builds first wins. 2026-06-21T17-05 run re-flagged the SAME class: --output is registered by BOTH purify and review on the unified image parser. (2) None-sentinel poison: image-profile registers --seed with default=None as a sentinel — because profile's parser is the FIRST/only writer on a shared dest across ALL image sub-actions on the unified parser, default=None leaks into every image sub-action's --seed. The 2026-06-22T00-55 run re-flagged the EXACT profile --seed default=None finding AGAIN (argparse-integrity-image-profile.py-153, high) — the None-sentinel persists across runs unfixed. (3) inline magic-number compare: video-generate._apply_prompt_defaults magic-number compares cfg_scale/stg_scale against the WRONG argparse defaults. (4) dest-name dodge (2026-06-22T13-49 run, argparse-integrity-video-t2i2v-63, low): video-t2i2v registers --action with dest=vlm_action to AVOID colliding with the shared 'action' dest that video.py's positional 'action' subcommand selector uses — the dodge is fragile because it silently couples t2i2v's flag name to video.py's positional naming. (5) sentinel-only recommended-default check (2026-06-22T20-14 run, correctness-video-generate-511, medium): video-generate's self-test recommended defaults for frames/width/height/fps are applied via a sentinel-ONLY check (default=None compare) against the concrete argparse defaults — the recommended values are silently never applied because the argparse defaults are concrete numbers (not None), so the sentinel predicate never matches. Root cause unifies all five: the source-of-truth for a flag's default/dest is argparse, but shared dests across sub-actions collide and the collision is worked around with sentinels, registration-order reliance, dest renames, or sentinel-vs-concrete mismatches that drift. The None-sentinel also enables a SIBLING falsy-coalesce bug (see gotcha:numeric-falsy-coalesce-overrides-explicit-zero). Fix: never re-state a default inline; resolve the value explicitly per sub-action at runtime from a fresh local (never store the sentinel in the shared dest); do not rely on registration order or on None-as-skip; register shared flags in exactly ONE place; prefer a dedicated dest over dest=aliasing a shared positional; and when applying recommended defaults, compare against the concrete argparse default value, not a None-sentinel. Found via review scans. (6) 2026-06-26T05-33 run re-flagged the family THREE times on the unified IMAGE parser: (a) image-profile.py-153 (LOW, argparse-integrity) — --seed default=None from profile STILL wins over _shared's intended default=777 on the unified IMAGE parser (the SAME None-sentinel-poison locus flagged at 22-00-55, 22-20-14; now downgraded high->low but unfixed across 3 runs); (b) image-t2i.py-62 (LOW) — --width/--height/--resolution/--transformer are registered UNGUARDED (no _arg_registered) so their correctness depends ENTIRELY on image.add_args() calling add_t2i_args() FIRST in the registration order — load-bearing registration order is the undocumented-contract face; (c) image-purify.py-95 (LOW) — --resolution/--transformer/--seed/--film-grain/--sharpening in purify are guard-skipped so purify's OWN defaults (seed=42, transformer=klein-9b, resolution='same') are MASKED by whichever sibling built first, the masked-defaults face. And (d) image.py-225 (INFO) names the ROOT: image add_args() registers 16 sibling add_*_args() functions on ONE parser; registration order is load-bearing and undocumented as a contract — the family's process-level root cause is that a single parser accumulates 16 sibling writers with no declared ordering invariant. Confirms the first-writer-wins / None-sentinel / unguarded-registration / load-bearing-order faces all co-occur on the unified IMAGE parser and persist across 8 runs unfixed.

title: Bare subprocess.run/Popen without FileNotFoundError/Timeout handling hangs or wraps a crash in an unhelpful traceback; missing-timeout is the forever-hang variant; un-captured child output + downstream file-read is the silent-empty variant; inline-opened stdout handle is the fd-leak variant
detail: Bare subprocess calls on external binaries (ffmpeg/ffprobe/transformer-backend CLI / long-running server child) need uniform guarding. Confirmed variants. (1) video-relay._extract_last_frame calls subprocess.run([ffmpeg,...]) with capture_output=True, timeout=60 but no try/except; the SECOND call IS wrapped against TimeoutExpired but the FIRST is NOT — asymmetric guarding is the easy-to-miss form. (2) 2026-06-21T17-05 run flagged image-purify transformer-backend Popen (medium, error-handling) with NO timeout — if the child stalls the parent hangs FOREVER. (3) 2026-06-22T12-33 run re-flagged the Popen variant in video-review (medium): a Popen that spawns a server child leaves stdout file handle NEVER closed AND the server process NEVER reaped / NEVER given a timeout. (4) 2026-06-23T00-13 run re-flagged the Popen stdout-leak variant in quality_metrics.py (medium): subprocess.Popen opens a stdout file handle via open() that is NEVER closed, and the call has NO timeout/kill — so a stalling child hangs forever AND the fd leaks even on a clean exit. (5) 2026-06-23T11-49 run flagged a NEW face in video-t2i2v (low): the VLM subprocess.run streams child stdout/stderr straight to the PARENT (no capture); the call HAS a timeout and a returncode guard, but because output is un-captured the downstream code reads vlm_output WITHOUT confirming the child actually wrote it — the un-captured-child + downstream-file-read-race face. (6) 2026-06-24T01-26 run re-flagged the quality_metrics Popen stdout-leak variant AGAIN (medium, error-handling-quality_metrics-281): Popen opens a stdout file handle INLINE that is never closed — the SAME locus flagged at 00-13, now in its SECOND run unfixed; AND added the missing-FileNotFoundError face in video-relay._mux_audio_track (low, error-handling-video-relay-531): subprocess.run has no FileNotFoundError guard, so a missing ffmpeg after _require_ffmpeg could still raise uncaught — confirms the missing-binary-guard face that the family title has long advertised but that had not been concretely located until now. Pattern: any subprocess.run/Popen on a possibly-missing or possibly-stalling external binary must (a) catch FileNotFoundError and emit a guided install hint, (b) pass a timeout and catch TimeoutExpired to degrade, (c) wrap uniformly across all calls in the helper (don't guard the second and forget the first), (d) for long-lived children (servers) explicitly close inherited stdout/stderr handles and reap/terminate the child on exit, AND (e) when the child writes a separate output file that the parent later reads, GUARD the read with an existence + non-empty-size check. Missing-timeout and no-reap are the silent-forever-hang / orphan-process variants — worse than a crash because they produce no traceback. Popen's stdout=open(...) handle is a SECOND fd that must be closed independently of reaping the child. (7) 2026-06-26T05-33 run added TWO more faces: (a) the readline-forever-hang face in image-purify (correctness-image-purify-444, HIGH): the transformer-backend child's stdout is consumed via readline() with NO timeout, so a hung/stalled child blocks the parent INDEFINITELY — defeating even a 30-min deadline because the parent is wedged in the blocking read, not in a wait() the deadline can interrupt; this is the forever-hang variant made concrete at the readline (not wait) layer. (b) the silent-degrade face in gpu_monitor (error-handling-gpu-monitor-73, MEDIUM): macmon is invoked as a streaming/long-lived subprocess ('pipe -s 1 -i 500') UNDER a 4s timeout, so a slow/streaming macmon that needs longer than 4s is silently killed and GPU detection falls back to the heuristic tiers with NO signal that the authoritative probe was discarded — the missing-timeout family's inverse: here the timeout EXISTS but is too aggressive for a streaming child, so the guard itself causes the silent degradation. Confirms the family spans 8 modules; readline()-on-a-child-stream is a NEW surface (the blocking-read layer, not wait()/Popen.communicate), and a too-short timeout on a streaming child is as silent as no timeout.

title: A handle released on the happy path (cap.release()/Image.close()) is leaked if any later line raises; try/finally / context-manager is mandatory for cv2/file/PIL handles; json.load(open()) and long-lived PIL are the no-exception-needed faces
detail: cv2.VideoCapture/VideoWriter (and any OS handle) and PIL Image opened then released/closed only on the success path leaks the handle / leaves the file locked when any line between open and release raises. Confirmed across multiple command modules: video-segment opens VideoCapture, reads metadata, then calls cap.release() — but only on the success path. video-restore opens BOTH cv2.VideoCapture and a VideoWriter without try/finally — a later exception leaks both handles (re-flagged at the 2026-06-22T00-55 run, medium). The 2026-06-22T00-55 run ALSO added the PIL face: image-quality opens comparison images via Image.open WITHOUT a context manager, leaking the fd across the comparison-image list (low). The 2026-06-22T00-10 run re-flagged the cv2 face AGAIN in video_utils (medium): OpenCV VideoCapture opened, then cap.get() called before cap.release() — if cap.get() raises on a corrupt video the handle is leaked. The 2026-06-22T13-49 run added a NEW long-lived-PIL face (low, correctness-image-i2i-843): the self-test keeps source_pil (a PIL Image) OPEN across the long VAE encode loop. The 2026-06-22T20-14 run re-flagged the PIL face in TWO MORE loci: _shared.execute_ab_test opens comparison images WITHOUT context managers (low); and video-generate._prepare_i2v_image opens Image WITHOUT a context manager (low). The 2026-06-23T00-13 run added FOUR MORE loci across three handle families: video_utils extract_keyframes loop opens cv2.VideoCapture WITHOUT try/finally (medium); video-quality.analyze_video opens cv2.VideoCapture then calls sys.exit(1) INSIDE the body (medium) — the sys.exit short-circuits before cap.release(); image-quality batch list-comprehension Image.open() WITHOUT context manager (low); image-review per-image loop open(path,'rb').read() (medium) — the raw file fd leaks each iteration. The 2026-06-23T11-49 run added TWO MORE faces: (a) json.load(open(path)) — the classic one-liner fd leak (low): open() is passed straight into json.load with no reference held, so the file is never explicitly closed; (b) image-i2i self-test variation loop opens Image.open(source_path).convert(...).resize(...) WITHOUT a context manager (medium) — source_pil is held across the VAE encode of every variation. Confirms the class spans 12 modules and that json.load(open()) is the no-exception-needed face — the leak happens on EVERY call, not just on the error path. General trap: a happy-path release()/close() is not resource safety, a long-lived open Image is a latent leak even without an exception, a sys.exit() inside a handle scope is a hidden fd leak, AND `json.load(open(x))` leaks unconditionally. Prefer with/contextlib.closing (or try/finally) so the release is exception-safe, for cv2 handles AND PIL Image objects AND any file opened for the duration of a loop AND the open()-inside-json.load idiom; for long loops, close/re-open or scope the Image to the minimal block; and NEVER call sys.exit() between a handle open and its release — raise a typed exception instead so context-manager cleanup runs. Found via review-only scans.

title: A command module that fully implements the contract (PARSER_META/add_args/run) but is absent from COMMAND_NAMES is unreachable — and can silently dispatch the WRONG model if a name shadows a live one
detail: animate.py implements PARSER_META, add_args(parser), and run(args) — the full command module contract — yet 'animate' is NOT in cli.COMMAND_NAMES nor in COMMAND_ALIASES. So build_parser never registers it. Re-flagged TWO findings in the 2026-06-21T00-10 run (a low and a medium, both naming animate.py); the 2026-06-22T00-10 run re-flagged animate.py AGAIN with TWO findings (low argparse-integrity-animate-46 + medium argparse-integrity-animate.py-7); the 2026-06-22T12-33 run escalated the SAME locus to HIGH (argparse-integrity-animate.py-1): the finding title now reads 'run.py animate silently dispatches the WRONG model' — i.e. the orphan is not merely an unknown command but actively routes to an unintended model, which is a correctness hazard (wrong output, silent), not just dead code. The orphan persists across 4 runs unfixed, confirming it was not patched. Trap: a module can pass every quality gate while being structurally unreachable (or worse, shadowing a live dispatch target). Guard: assert the module's name appears in COMMAND_NAMES (a one-line integrity test), and assert NO two registered command modules share a dispatch token, or delete the stub. The repo already has test_selftest_integrity.py for a parallel case (deleted-test references); a COMMAND_NAMES-membership assertion is the analog fix. Found via effort:low review-only scans (low 2026-06-20; low+medium 2026-06-21; low+medium 2026-06-22 00-10; HIGH 2026-06-22 12-33).

title: Help text that advertises a default the argparse default doesn't match, or a duplicate flag whose guarded twin is silently skipped, misleads users and reviewers
detail: Two related argparse-integrity gaps surfaced in the 2026-06-21T00-10 run. (1) Stale advertised default: image-t2i's help string advertises default 640/960, but the argparse default is None (the sentinel pattern) — a user reading --help is told a value is preset when it is not, and a reviewer reading help text cannot trust it as the source of truth. (2) Guarded-twin divergence: image-workflow registers --film-grain / --sharpening WITHOUT the _arg_registered guard, while image-purify registers guarded copies of the same flags — the guard dedupes and silently keeps only the FIRST (purify's) registration, so the workflow-specific help text/defaults never take effect even though they look wired. The 2026-06-22T00-10 run re-flagged the SAME class as stale COMMENT divergence (not just help text): video.py line ~115 has a comment claiming --self-test comes from add_common_generation_args() which video.py never calls (low), and image-purify.py has a stale guard comment claiming image-expansion registers --resolution when expansion does not. The 2026-06-22T20-14 run re-flagged the video.py stale-comment locus AGAIN (argparse-integrity-video.py-128, medium): the comment STILL claims add_common_generation_args() registers --self-test which video.py never calls — the stale comment persists across 3 runs unfixed and escalated from low to medium. The 2026-06-25T13-19 run re-flagged the SAME add_common_generation_args()--self-test stale-comment class for the FOURTH run, now as TWO sibling loci (both low): argparse-integrity-video.py-129 (the comment at video.py line ~129 STILL claims --self-test is registered via add_common_generation_args() which video.py never calls — the comment drifted by ONE line from 128 to 129 between runs, confirming the locus is unchanged) AND argparse-integrity-video-quality.py-112 (a NEW locus: video-quality.py's own comment at line ~112 ALSO claims --self-test is registered via add_common_generation_args() in video.py — the same false claim copy-pasted into a SECOND command module, so the stale comment has now SPREAD to a sibling file, not just persisted in one). The class now spans TWO command modules (video.py + video-quality.py) and has persisted across 4 runs unfixed; the false add_common_generation_args() claim is being copy-pasted between sibling quality/video sub-actions. The two are the same root cause: the comment/help/default surface and the actual argparse registration surface have drifted apart, and nothing asserts they agree. Fix: treat help text AND comments as a contract — add an integrity test that parses --help and asserts each flag's advertised default equals argparse's actual default; grep comments referencing functions to confirm the call exists; and for shared flags, register in exactly ONE place (canonical t2i/_shared) and never re-add unguarded in a sub-action. Found via effort:low review-only scans.

title: _arg_registered / _option_registered use parser._actions (a private argparse attribute) to detect prior registration — fragile across argparse versions
detail: app/commands/_shared._arg_registered and _option_registered check whether a flag is already registered by scanning parser._actions for matching option strings. parser._actions is an undocumented private attribute of argparse.ArgumentParser; its shape/contents are not part of the stable API and can change across Python versions or argparse refactors. A registration-guard built on a private attribute can silently mis-detect (false-negative -> duplicate-add crash; false-positive -> flag skipped) after a stdlib upgrade. Re-flagged at the 2026-06-22T00-55 run (low, argparse-integrity, app/commands/_shared.py _arg_registered / _option_registered locus) — confirms the private-attribute dependency persists. The robust check uses only documented behavior: wrap add_argument in try/except argparse.ArgumentError (the documented signal that an option string is already taken), or maintain an explicit set of registered dest/option-strings in the helper. Prefer the try/except-ArgumentError pattern — it relies only on argparse's documented behavior and needs no private-attribute access. Found via effort:low review-only scans (medium 2026-06-21T02-22; low 2026-06-22).

title: sys.path.insert(0, ...) in the entry module (run.py) matches the known KB 'sys.path.insert(0) in library modules' anti-pattern (milder in an entry module)
detail: run.py (the CLI entry point) calls sys.path.insert(0, ...) to make app/ importable. This matches the repo's existing KB guidance against sys.path.insert(0) manipulation. In an ENTRY module the risk is lower than in a library module (there is no caller whose sys.path gets polluted before its own imports), but the pattern still couples importability to CWD/launch path and hides the real packaging fix (a proper package install / pyproject.toml / console_scripts entry point). Prefer declaring the project as an installable package so run.py is reached via a console_script and app/ is importable without path mutation. Keep this distinct from the library-module variant (which is strictly worse because it poisons every importer). Found via effort:low review-only scan (low, run.py entry).

title: A loop body that reads args.* / shared dicts for every iteration aliases shared state across iterations instead of per-iteration copies; setattr'ing variation metadata onto the shared Namespace leaks it into downstream run.json; setting a per-variation field to the FULL dict (not the slice) misleads the manifest
detail: Per-iteration loops that read shared argparse args or shared dicts alias state across iterations: if any iteration (or the called pipeline) mutates the object in place (append to a list field, set an attribute, cache by identity), subsequent iterations see the mutated state — cross-variant contamination invisible when each variant is independent but catastrophic if a frame/image is cached by identity. Confirmed loci: video-generate's A/B variation generate() uses args.input_image / args.audio for ALL variants (medium 2026-06-21T02-22). 2026-06-21T17-05 run re-flagged the SAME class in TWO new loci: video-relay variant loop mutates shared args object (copy.copy is a SHALLOW copy — nested dicts/lists still alias; medium, correctness, video-relay), and run_config.py ab_params is typed as dict but shared across A/B variations without deep copy (medium, correctness, run_config). The 2026-06-22T00-55 run re-flagged the run_config.py ab_params locus AGAIN (low, type-safety). The 2026-06-22T12-33 run re-flagged the class TWICE more: (a) video-generate FLF2V A/B variation loop ignores var_args.end_image resolution and reuses the shared begin/end paths for every variant (medium, correctness-video-generate-491); (b) run_config.py ab_params typed dict[str,Any] but _resolve_ab_params can receive list-valued JSON (low, type-safety-run-config-132). The 2026-06-22T13-49 run re-flagged the CORE video-generate locus AGAIN (medium, correctness-video-generate-935): _run_variations MUTATES args.input_image IN PLACE, poisoning _run_single AND any later replay — the ESCAPED-MUTATION face. The 2026-06-23T11-49 run re-flagged the SAME video-generate variation loop with a NEW face (low, argparse-integrity-video-generate-990): _run_variations setattr's variation_index / ab_params_json / pipeline onto the shared var_args Namespace — these bookkeeping attributes then LEAK into the run.json, the METADATA-LEAK face. The 2026-06-24T01-26 run re-flagged the SAME video-generate variation loop with the SLICE-OMISSION face (low, correctness-video-generate-994): var_args.ab_params_json is set to the FULL ab_params dict rather than the per-variation slice — run.json metadata is correct (the resolved slice is what runs) but the bookkeeping attr on the Namespace is misleading, so a replay or manifest-diff tool reading var_args.ab_params_json sees the whole dict instead of the single variation. Confirms the trap spans video-relay + run_config + video-generate (FLF2V + A/B + escaped mutation + metadata leak + slice omission) — shallow copy.copy is NOT enough, the typed-dict annotation gives false safety, setattr'ing bookkeeping onto the Namespace leaks it into run.json, AND setting a metadata field to the aggregate instead of the slice misleads downstream readers. Fix: deep-copy or freshly resolve per-iteration inputs at the top of each loop body (copy.deepcopy(args.input_image) / re-read from source), validate JSON shape before storing into a typed field, treat the shared args Namespace as IMMUTABLE inside any loop (never setattr/assign back onto it, including for metadata), carry per-variation metadata in a side-channel that does not flow into RunConfig.from_args, AND when recording a per-variation bookkeeping field, record the per-variation SLICE (not the aggregate dict). Static analysis rarely catches this because the read looks read-only. Found via review scans.

title: ffmpeg -sseof -N (seek-from-end) fails or mis-extracts on segments shorter than N seconds
detail: video-relay._extract_last_frame invokes ffmpeg with -sseof -3 (seek 3s before end-of-file) to grab the last frame. On segments shorter than 3s the -sseof offset lands before the start and ffmpeg either errors or extracts the wrong frame, silently breaking last-frame extraction for short clips. Pattern: any ffmpeg seek-from-end (-sseof) or duration-dependent flag must clamp the offset to the actual media duration (probe with ffprobe first, or compute min(offset, duration)). Do NOT assume a fixed -sseof offset is valid for all inputs — short segments are the edge case that breaks it. Fix: ffprobe the duration, clamp the seek offset, and fall back to extracting the final frame by index when the segment is shorter than the offset. Found via review scan (medium, correctness, video-relay._extract_last_frame).

title: `value or DEFAULT` falsy-coalesces explicit 0/0.0/empty into DEFAULT — silent override for numeric args where 0 is valid
detail: Reading a numeric arg as `x = args.x or DEFAULT` treats an EXPLICIT user-supplied 0 (or 0.0, or empty string) as 'unset' and silently substitutes DEFAULT — the caller's explicit value is lost with no error. This is the runtime-side twin of the default=None sentinel poison (gotcha:argparse-shared-flag-default-bleeds-first-writer-wins): the sentinel makes None mean 'unset', and the falsy-coalesce makes 0 mean 'unset', so BOTH None and 0 are mis-read. Confirmed loci: 2026-06-22T00-55 run — image-quality seed handling `seed = args.seed or DEFAULT` overrides an explicit --seed 0 (medium, correctness); image-profile run_meta lora_scale falsy-coerce overrides an explicit 0.0 (medium, correctness — list-typed input makes it doubly wrong, intersecting gotcha:lora-multi-flag-list-vs-scalar). 2026-06-22T00-10 run re-flagged the SAME class in video-t2i2v (medium, correctness-video-t2i2v-71): an `or` pattern overrides an explicit --seed 0 to 99. 2026-06-22T13-49 run re-flagged in TWO MORE loci: (a) run_config.from_args uses `input_image ... or getattr(args, 'input', None)` (medium) — the `or` silently drops an explicit-but-falsy input_image; (b) _shared.seed_sequence uses `count = ... or 1` (low) which treats an explicit --count 0 as 1. The 2026-06-22T20-14 run re-flagged the run_config.from_args locus AGAIN (low, argparse-integrity-run_config-217): empty-string input_image ('') falls back to args.input unexpectedly. The 2026-06-24T01-26 run re-flagged the class with the FPS=0 face in video-generate (high, correctness-video-generate-722): the fps falsy-check (`fps or DEFAULT`) treats an explicit --fps 0 as unset and substitutes the default — so a user who legitimately requests fps=0 (or a caller passing 0 to mean 'no frame-rate override') gets silently overridden; fps=0 is the multiplicative/identity case of the same family (0 is a valid explicit value the coalesce clobbers). Confirms the class now spans image-quality + image-profile + video-t2i2v + run_config + _shared + video-generate (6 modules) across 5 runs; the run_config locus specifically re-fires on the empty-STRING face (not just 0/None) — falsy-coalesce is wrong for strings/paths too. Fix: always use identity-unset semantics `x if x is not None else DEFAULT` for numeric args where 0/0.0 is a valid explicit value; NEVER use truthiness (`or`) as the 'was it provided' test for numbers — and for string/path args prefer an explicit None-sentinel check, not truthiness. The falsy-coalesce class is distinct from the None-sentinel registration trap but the two co-occur and amplify each other. Found via effort:low review-only scans.

title: Pipeline events left embedded in the timings dict are lost to callers and pollute the timing record
detail: video-generate._run_single (correctness-video-generate-891, high) captures LTX pipeline timing into a timings dict but never LIFTS the LTX events out of that dict — the events stay embedded inside the timings record, so (a) event consumers never see them (events are effectively lost), and (b) the timings dict is polluted with event data that should live in a separate events structure. General trap: when a helper returns a composite dict carrying BOTH timings AND structured events, failing to destructure/lift the events at the boundary means every downstream consumer that reads timings gets corrupted metrics, and every event consumer gets nothing. Fix: explicitly extract events into their own field/return-value at the boundary (events = timings.pop('events', []) or a separate return slot), and assert in a test that timings contains no event keys. Distinct from gotcha:loop-shared-args-state-mutation (which is cross-iteration aliasing) — this is a single-return-value destructuring omission. Found via effort:low review-only scan (high, correctness, video-generate).

title: A context-manager __enter__ / lock-acquire except clause that catches too broadly (BaseException OR plain Exception) masks unexpected acquisition errors or swallows control-flow signals; paired with an fd-open-in-__enter__ it leaks the fd
detail: A lock/context-manager __enter__ that catches broadly 'to clean up on any failure' over-catches. Two confirmed faces. (1) BaseException: video-generate GpuLock.__enter__ (correctness-video-generate-410 / error-handling, low) wraps the acquire in an except clause catching BaseException subclasses broader than intended — catching BaseException (or bare except, which in py3 catches BaseException) swallows KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, and GeneratorExit, preventing clean Ctrl-C / interpreter-shutdown / generator-teardown signals from propagating. (2) Plain Exception: gpu_monitor.py GpuLock.__enter__ (error-handling-gpu_monitor-431, low) catches Exception — less severe than BaseException but STILL risks masking unexpected acquisition errors (e.g. a real lock-corruption / flock-EBADF) as a benign 'failed to acquire' retry. The 2026-06-22T12-33 run confirms the over-catch is now in TWO modules (video-generate + gpu_monitor), both GpuLock.__enter__. The 2026-06-22T20-14 run re-flagged the gpu_monitor.py GpuLock locus (correctness-gpu_monitor-407, medium) with a NEW but related face: GpuLock.__enter__ opens the lock fd but __exit__ does NOT run if the body raises — fd leak on exception. The 2026-06-23T00-13 run re-flagged the gpu_monitor.py GpuLock locus AGAIN (error-handling-gpu_monitor-407, low): __enter__ opens the lock fd but only closes it for 3 NARROW exception types — any UNEXPECTED exception leaks the fd AND the held process reference. The 2026-06-23T11-49 run re-flagged the gpu_monitor.py GpuLock locus a FOURTH time (correctness-gpu_monitor-407, low): the fd is opened BEFORE the flock retry loop, the advisory detect_gpu_busy() runs each poll but the real mutex is flock, yet the fd is NOT closed on BaseException. This is the resource-safety sibling of the over-broad-catch family: the lock wrapper promises cleanup via __exit__ but if __enter__'s narrow except list misses the actual failure class, the fd is never closed. Fix: inside __enter__ catch only the SPECIFIC expected failure, NOT Exception and NOT BaseException; ensure __exit__ closes the lock fd UNCONDITIONALLY (defensive, independent of the except list in __enter__), and put cleanup in __exit__ via the documented context-manager protocol; open the fd inside the try (or ensure __exit__ always closes it) so an exception before flock still releases the fd. Bare `except:` is equivalent to `except BaseException:` in py3 — always name the exception class you intend, AND separate the fd-close from the exception-matching so a missed exception still releases the fd. Pair with gotcha:resource-handle-release-skipped-on-exception. Found via effort:low review-only scans.

title: One metric aliased to another (motion_mean = flicker_mean) makes a 'has X' gate fire on the wrong signal — it never fires independently
detail: video-t2i2v (correctness-video-t2i2v-300, medium): motion_mean is computed as an ALIAS of flicker_mean (same value / same source), so a downstream 'has motion' gate that is supposed to branch on motion strength is actually branching on flicker — the motion gate never fires independently of flicker. The bug is invisible to a reader because both names look like distinct metrics, and a test that exercises the gate under a motion-only / flicker-only scenario is the only thing that exposes it. General trap: when two metrics share a name relationship (alias, copy, or one derived purely from the other without an independent signal), any gate predicated on the aliased metric is really predicated on its source — the semantic the gate advertises (motion) is not the semantic it evaluates (flicker). Fix: give each metric an independent computation/source, OR rename the gate to match what it actually tests (has_flicker), OR delete the dead alias; add a test that drives the aliased metric with motion-only input (flicker held constant) and asserts the gate responds. Distinct from gotcha:events-left-in-timings-dict (data lost) — here the metric exists but carries the wrong signal. Found via effort:low review-only scan (medium, correctness, video-t2i2v).

title: A pad-list helper that repeats the LAST element silently injects a duplicate frame/scale where a neutral default (1.0 / copy-last-frame) is expected
detail: video-generate._scale_list (correctness-video-generate-413, low): when padding a list of per-frame scales to the frame count, the helper REPEATS THE LAST SCALE for the missing slots instead of defaulting to a neutral 1.0 (no-scale). Net effect: trailing frames get the last specified scale applied even though the caller intended 'no further scaling past the end' — a silent semantic shift where the pad value is data-derived (the last input) rather than a neutral identity. The bug is easy to miss because repeating-the-last is a common pad idiom and only looks wrong when the last scale is far from 1.0. General trap: padding a sequence with a DATA-DERIVED value (repeat-last, repeat-first) rather than a NEUTRAL/IDENTITY default (1.0 for scales, 0.0 for offsets, a copy of the last frame for frame-padding) silently changes the meaning of the padded region — the padded tail behaves like the last input, not like the identity. Fix: pad with the semantically-neutral default for the quantity (1.0 for multiplicative scales, or document + assert that repeat-last is intended); add a test that pads a list ending in a non-1.0 scale and asserts the padded slots equal the neutral default. Found via effort:low review-only scan (low, correctness, video-generate).

title: A finally/cleanup `del a, b, c` raises UnboundLocalError when the loop body conditionally skipped binding one of the names
detail: app/pipeline.py Phase-4 cleanup (correctness-pipeline-571, medium) runs `del model, scheduler, step_fn, cos_cached, sin_cached` to release memory, but step_fn is bound INSIDE the denoising loop body and a code path where the loop body never executes (or skips the binding branch) leaves step_fn UNBOUND — the `del` then raises UnboundLocalError, masking the original outcome and crashing the cleanup. General trap: a cleanup block (finally / explicit del / context-manager __exit__) that names variables bound INSIDE a conditional/loop body will UnboundLocalError whenever that body was skipped (zero-iteration loop, an early-continue, an if-branch not taken, an exception before the assignment). The cleanup was written assuming every name is always bound, which only holds on the happy path. Related to gotcha:resource-handle-release-skipped-on-exception (happy-path-only release) but the failure mode here is the inverse — the cleanup RUNS but references a never-bound name. Fix: initialize every name to None (or a sentinel) BEFORE the conditional body so the del is always safe (`step_fn = None` before the loop; `del` of a None-bound name is a no-op), or guard the cleanup with `if 'step_fn' in locals()`, or prefer a context manager / try-finally whose cleanup does not name loop-body locals. Static analysis misses this because the del looks balanced. Found via effort:low review-only scan (medium, correctness, app/pipeline.py Phase-4 cleanup).

title: A helper that setattr's arbitrary JSON object keys onto the argparse Namespace with no validation injects unknown attributes / overrides internals
detail: video-generate._override_args (correctness-video-generate-1159, medium) trusts arbitrary keys from --ab-params JSON and setattr's each onto the args Namespace with NO allowlist/validation. An unknown or mistyped key silently becomes a new attribute on the Namespace (harmless-looking junk) OR — worse — OVERWRITES a real argparse dest (e.g. a key named 'seed' or 'input_image' clobbers the user's CLI value), and a key whose value has the wrong type passes straight through to the pipeline as a typed kwarg, crashing far from the injection point. General trap: reflecting untrusted JSON keys onto a Namespace/dataclass via setattr turns the JSON object schema into an implicit, unchecked extension of the CLI surface — there is no contract between what the JSON may contain and what the Namespace is allowed to hold. This is the args-mutation sibling of gotcha:loop-shared-args-state-mutation (both write onto the shared Namespace) but the injection vector here is EXTERNAL untrusted input (a JSON file) rather than an internal loop. Fix: validate the JSON object against an explicit allowlist of overridable keys (reject unknown keys with a clear error), type-check each value against the argparse dest's expected type, and prefer a dedicated dataclass (Overlay / ABParams) for the JSON payload rather than reflecting onto the live Namespace — never setattr an untrusted key onto the object that downstream pipeline calls read from. Found via effort:low review-only scan (medium, correctness, app/commands/video-generate.py _override_args).

title: ffmpeg arg ORDER for -ar/-ac vs the input determines whether the requested sample-rate/channel-count applies — mis-ordered flags silently produce empty or wrong-rate output
detail: app/audio_noise_detect._extract_audio_pcm (correctness-audio_noise_detect-54, medium, 2026-06-22T13-49 run) builds the ffmpeg command so that the -ar (audio sample rate) / -ac (audio channels) output flags are placed in a branch that mis-orders them relative to the -i input and the codec args, so when a NON-native sample rate is requested ffmpeg emits an EMPTY output file (0 bytes) instead of the resampled PCM. The 2026-06-23T00-13 run re-flagged the EXACT SAME locus (correctness-audio_noise_detect-54, low) — the ffmpeg -ar/-ac sample_rate-insert mis-order persists across 2 runs unfixed, confirming the arg-order bug was not patched. The extraction then 'succeeds' (ffmpeg exit 0) but the downstream reader gets nothing — a silent empty-output failure worse than a crash because there is no traceback. General trap: ffmpeg applies output-options (-ar/-ac/-acodec/-af) to the NEXT output file and they are position-sensitive relative to -i; placing an output option BEFORE -i makes ffmpeg treat it as an input option (often ignored or erroring), and placing -ar after the wrong token can make the resampling a no-op that still exits 0. The mis-order is invisible in a string-concat command builder because all flags look present. Fix: build ffmpeg commands with a strict section order [global opts] -i <input> [input-specific opts] <output> [output opts: -ar/-ac/-acodec/-af], place ALL output-format options together AFTER the output path token, and assert the output file is non-empty (os.path.getsize > 0) after the call — treat a 0-byte output as a hard failure even when ffmpeg exits 0. Related to gotcha:ffmpeg-sseof-fails-on-short-segments (both are silent ffmpeg mis-extraction classes) but the root cause here is flag ordering, not duration. Found via effort:low review-only scans.

title: VLM score-style responses parsed without KeyError/IndexError guard crash when the model omits/reshapes a field; a SECOND call path repeats the unguarded parse
detail: app/commands/caption.py (correctness-caption-1145, high, 2026-06-23T00-13 run): a VLM score-style JSON response is accessed without a KeyError/IndexError guard on a SECOND call path — the first path was presumably hardened but the second call path re-introduces the unguarded dict/list access. VLM models (Qwen3-VL / Gemma VL) intermittently omit fields, return them under a different key, or wrap scores in a nested list when the prompt phrasing shifts, so any `resp['score']` / `resp[0]` access without a .get()/try-except crashes the whole caption/review on a model that returned a valid-but-differently-shaped response. General trap: when a VLM response is consumed by MORE THAN ONE call path (e.g. score-mode vs caption-mode vs a retry loop), the hardening must be applied to EVERY path, not just the primary one — a copy-pasted call site silently inherits the unguarded parse. Fix: centralize VLM-response parsing in ONE helper (parse_vlm_score(resp) -> Optional[float]) that uses .get() with a fallback and validates the shape, and route ALL call paths through it; add a test that feeds a field-omitted / list-wrapped / wrong-key response and asserts the helper degrades gracefully rather than crashing. Pair with the known repo VLM-over-praise QA gap (VLM responses are prompt-unstable, so shape variance is the rule not the exception). Found via effort:low review-only scan (high, correctness, app/commands/caption.py).

title: Review lane fabricated a NameError by claiming a variable is bound only inside an if-branch when it is actually bound BEFORE the if/else — scope misread
detail: 2026-06-23T11-49 run scored a HIGH argparse-integrity finding (argparse-integrity-image-profile.py-830): 'NameError: resolved_lora referenced in the else branch but only defined inside the use_flux2 branch.' VERIFIED FALSE: in app/commands/image-profile.py the line `resolved_lora = (resolve_lora_paths(getattr(args, 'lora_path', None)) or [None])[0]` executes BEFORE the `if use_flux2: ... else: ...` block, so resolved_lora is bound in BOTH branches and no NameError can occur. The review agent misread the control flow — it treated a pre-conditional assignment as if it lived inside the if-branch. This is the variable-SCOPE variant of the review-lane misdiagnosis family (the project KB already documents review findings whose symptom is real but root cause is misdiagnosed; here the symptom itself is fabricated — there is no bug at all). General trap: a review finding that names a NameError/UnboundLocalError on a variable used in BOTH branches of an if/else is very often a SCOPE misread — the agent assumed the binding was conditional when it was unconditional (pre-if). Before acting on such a finding, GREP the variable name and confirm whether the assignment is INSIDE the branch or BEFORE it; a pre-conditional assignment makes the finding a false positive. This one survived adversarial-verify as 'upheld' — adversarial-verify does NOT re-check basic Python scope, so a scope-misread NameError sails through both lanes. Discriminate from a REAL NameError (where the grep shows the binding genuinely missing from one branch) by the grep, not by the finding's confidence. Do NOT auto-apply a fix for a NameError finding without grepping the binding site.

title: An A/B variation loop that keeps an IDENTICAL seed across variants by default has a comment claiming 'fairness' but it silently kills the diversity signal the A/B is meant to measure
detail: app/commands/video-generate.py _run_variations (correctness-video-generate-1192, low, 2026-06-23T11-49 run): the A/B variation generate loop keeps the SAME seed for every variant unless the user explicitly varies it via --ab-params, and a code comment claims this is 'for fairness'. The intent is defensible (same seed isolates the varied lever from seed noise), but the side-effect is that every variant is seeded identically, so an A/B whose varied knob is weak produces near-identical outputs and the diversity signal collapses — a reviewer or a self-improving loop reading the A/B delta sees almost no spread and cannot rank the variants. The comment over-claims 'fairness' while under-advertising the diversity cost. General trap: when an A/B/fairness loop pins an input (seed, prompt, reference) across variants for isolatability, the pin ALSO suppresses the very variance the comparison is meant to surface — a pinned-seed A/B can only differentiate variants whose lever is strong enough to overcome the zero-variance floor, so weak levers look inert and get wrongly dropped. Fix: either document the trade-off in the comment ('pinned seed isolates the lever but suppresses diversity — vary --seed-start for a diversity-spread A/B'), OR default the variation loop to a seed-offset per variant (--seed-start increments) so each variant is reproducible AND diverse, and let the user opt INTO a pinned-seed fairness A/B via an explicit flag. Distinct from gotcha:loop-shared-args-state-mutation (cross-iteration aliasing) — here the values are intentionally shared, the bug is the comment/semantics gap, not state contamination. Found via effort:low review-only scan (low, correctness, video-generate).

title: A typed-field coerce that int(True) on a JSON bool annotated 'int' silently yields 1 — the bool is accepted as a valid int with no error and the original intent (a flag) is lost
detail: app/run_config.py _coerce_typed_fields (correctness-run_config-468, medium, 2026-06-24T01-26 run): when run.json carries a JSON bool (true/false) for a field whose dataclass annotation is 'int', the coerce helper calls int(value) which happily returns 1 for True and 0 for False — Python's int() accepts bool because bool is a subclass of int. So a manifest that carries e.g. `"enable_x": true` for a field annotated int is silently accepted as 1 with no type error, and the original boolean intent is lost (the value is now an integer, not a flag). The bug is invisible because int(True) is syntactically legal and the round-trip looks plausible, but it violates the manifest's type contract (the field says int, the source said bool) and a downstream consumer that re-serializes or compares against the declared type has no signal that a bool slipped in. General trap: a coerce helper that maps JSON -> typed fields via a blanket int()/float()/str() call inherits Python's numeric-tower coercion, so bool (a subclass of int) passes the int() check silently — any type-validated manifest reader that assumes 'annotated int means the source was an int' is wrong for bool sources. This is the type-coercion sibling of gotcha:numeric-falsy-coalesce-overrides-explicit-zero (both are silent numeric coercion bugs) but the failure mode is ACCEPT-AS-VALID rather than OVERRIDE-WITH-DEFAULT: the coalesce clobbers an explicit value, the int(True) coerces an out-of-contract value into the declared type. Fix: in any JSON-to-typed-field coerce, explicitly REJECT bool when the target annotation is int/float (check `isinstance(value, bool)` BEFORE int()/float() and raise a clear type error, since bool is a subclass of int and must be excluded explicitly), OR annotate boolean fields as bool (not int) so the contract matches the source. Add a test that feeds a JSON bool into an int-annotated field and asserts the helper rejects it. Found via effort:low review-only scan (medium, correctness, app/run_config.py).

title: zip(list_a, list_b) silently truncates to the SHORTER list when the two differ in length — paired diagnostics/parallel collections drop entries with no error
detail: app/gpu_monitor.py (correctness-gpu_monitor-487, low, 2026-06-24T01-26 run): a busy/timeout report builds `zip(blocking_pids, blocking_commands)` to pair each blocking PID with its command — but if blocking_pids and blocking_commands have different lengths (one query returned fewer rows than the other, a filter dropped an entry from only one list, a race added a process to one list between the two queries), zip() silently stops at the SHORTER list and the trailing entries of the longer list are DROPPED with no error. The report then shows fewer blocking processes than actually exist, or mismatches a PID with the wrong command if the lists are misaligned rather than merely different-length. The bug is invisible because zip() is the idiomatic pairing call and produces no warning on length mismatch. General trap: zip() defaults to shortest-input truncation (only itertools.zip_longest pads), so ANY two parallel collections (pids+commands, names+values, keys+rows, headers+columns) zipped under the assumption they are equal-length will silently drop trailing entries when they diverge — and the divergence is often a symptom of an upstream race or partial query failure that itself deserves surfacing, not hiding. This is the silent-drop sibling of gotcha:bare-ternary-statement-discards-result (both discard data with no error) but the mechanism is zip's shortest-wins semantics, not a void-context ternary. Fix: when zipping two collections that MUST be equal-length, ASSERT len(a) == len(b) before the zip (or use itertools.zip_longest with a fillvalue and a post-loop check for the sentinel) so a length mismatch raises instead of silently truncating; for diagnostic/reporting code especially, a dropped entry means a missing or misattributed diagnosis. Found via effort:low review-only scan (low, correctness, app/gpu_monitor.py).

title: A derived quantity (duration_s / frame-count display) computed from frames BEFORE _adjust_frames ran on args uses the pre-adjustment value — the displayed/computed number diverges from what the pipeline actually used
detail: video-generate (correctness-video-generate-722, high + correctness-video-generate-842, medium, 2026-06-24T01-26 run): two faces of the same pre-vs-post-adjustment divergence. (1) duration_s is computed as frames/fps using the frames value BEFORE _adjust_frames adjusted args.frames (the adjustment to the 8-aligned minimum happens elsewhere or on a copy), so duration_s reflects the USER's requested frame count, not the frames the pipeline actually generated — the reported duration is wrong by the adjustment delta. Compounded by a missing fps falsy-check: if fps is 0 (see gotcha:numeric-falsy-coalesce-overrides-explicit-zero) the division is a ZeroDivisionError or an inf duration. (2) temporal-upscale frame-count display assumes a 2F-1 relationship but uses the PRE-temporal frame count, so the displayed 'final frame count' after temporal upscale does not match the actual upscaled output (which is computed from the post-adjustment base). General trap: any derived quantity that divides/displays/derives from a frame count MUST use the POST-adjustment value (the one the pipeline consumed), not the raw user value — otherwise every report/log/metric that quotes duration or frame count diverges from reality, and a ZeroDivisionError on fps=0 is the unguarded-division face. The pre/post divergence is invisible because both variables are named 'frames' in different scopes. This intersects gotcha:frame-floor-bypass-mod-predicate (the adjustment itself) and gotcha:numeric-falsy-coalesce-overrides-explicit-zero (the fps=0 face) but the root cause here is SCOPE: the derived math references the wrong (pre-adjustment) copy of the frame count. The 2026-06-25T13-19 run added the MANIFEST-RECORD face (correctness-video-generate-941, medium): the saved-output ctx record writes `"frames": frames` from the INPUT/pre-temporal frame count rather than the actual post-temporal-upscale OUTPUT frame count — so a reader of the output manifest (or a replay) sees the pre-upscale count and under-reports the real video length. This is the SAME scope-divergence as the 24-01 temporal-upscale frame-count DISPLAY face (the displayed/recorded number is the pre-upscale copy), now confirmed in the manifest-record locus as well as the display locus — any artifact that records the frame count for downstream consumption must thread the post-upscale value. Fix: compute duration_s and any frame-count display OR manifest record from the SAME post-adjustment / post-upscale frames variable the pipeline actually used (thread the adjusted value explicitly, never re-read from args.frames or a pre-upscale local after the upscale ran), and guard the fps division against fps falsy/zero (raise a clear error on fps=0 rather than dividing). Add a test that requests a non-8-aligned frame count, runs temporal upscale, and asserts duration_s == adjusted_frames/fps AND the manifest's frames field == the post-upscale output length. Found via effort:low review-only scans.

title: The lint lane (pyflakes real-bug hunt + check-model manifest + self-test registry) passes ALL THREE checks clean (zero real pyflakes bugs, manifest OK, self-test OK) as a stable baseline across runs — including lint-ONLY runs with no review lane; it is a structural-integrity backstop, not a defect finder
detail: 2026-06-23T22-40 run (lanes:[lint] ALONE, no review, openIssues=0): pyflakesRealCount=0, pyflakesIssues=[], checkModelOk=true, selftestOk=true — the lint lane's three structural checks all pass clean on a pure lint-only run. This re-confirms the baseline already noted in pattern:findings-cluster-on-boundary-modules ('Lint lane stays clean on code quality: pyflakesRealCount=0, checkModelOk=true, selftestOk=true across runs'). The lint lane is DETERMINISTIC (pyflakes real-bug filter, check-model manifest validation, self-test registry integrity test) and has stayed green across every recorded run regardless of whether the review lane runs — it catches import/registry/manifest STRUCTURAL breakage, not the latent runtime bugs the review lane surfaces (list-vs-scalar, falsy-coalesce, fd-leak, etc., which pyflakes structurally cannot see). Discriminator: a green lint lane does NOT imply code health — it only implies the structural contract (imports resolve, model manifest validates, self-test registry matches reality) holds; the review lane is the only lane that finds the runtime-correctness bugs. Do NOT treat openIssues=0 from a lint-only run as 'no bugs' — it means 'no STRUCTURAL bugs in the lint lane's scope'. Measured baseline for the lint-lane trifecta: pyflakesRealCount=0, checkModelOk=true, selftestOk=true.

title: A non-entry library module that calls sys.exit(1) on a missing-dependency guard (ffmpeg/ffprobe/binary) terminates the WHOLE process, preventing any caller from recovering, retrying, or degrading
detail: app/commands/video-relay.py _require_ffmpeg (error-handling-video-relay-430, MEDIUM, 2026-06-26T05-33 run) prints an install hint to stderr and calls sys.exit(1) when ffmpeg is missing — and its caller _concat_videos (and any other relay helper) invokes _require_ffmpeg, so the sys.exit propagates up through the library call stack and kills the interpreter. Because video-relay.py is a LIBRARY module (imported by cli/run.py, not the entry point), the sys.exit(1) bypasses every caller's exception handling: a caller that wanted to retry, fall back to an alternate muxer, or report a structured error cannot — the process is gone. sys.exit raises SystemExit (a BaseException subclass), so even a broad `except Exception` caller does NOT catch it. General trap: a missing-binary / missing-dependency guard in a non-entry module should RAISE a typed exception (FileNotFoundError / a custom MissingDependencyError) that the caller can catch and degrade from, NOT call sys.exit — sys.exit is reserved for the ENTRY module (run.py) where there is no caller to recover. The trap is invisible because the guard looks helpful (clear message + nonzero exit), but it converts a recoverable runtime condition into an unrecoverable process death. Sibling face: other command modules that call sys.exit(1) mid-body (see gotcha:resource-handle-release-skipped-on-exception's sys-exit-bypass face) are the same anti-pattern from the resource-safety angle — sys.exit inside a handle scope leaks the handle AND blocks caller recovery. Fix: in any non-entry module, replace sys.exit(1) on a dependency guard with `raise FileNotFoundError(...)` (or a dedicated MissingDependencyError) carrying the install hint as the message; reserve sys.exit for run.py / __main__ only. Add a test that asserts the guard raises (not sys.exits) when the binary is missing, so a caller's try/except can recover. Found via effort:low review-only scan.
